=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:1678-1692 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `granted` MERGE_LEASE_METRIC is emitted after `_merge_lease_unlabel_wait` (line 1686) and `_mt_dispatch_review` (line 1687), not right after the successful `_merge_lease_write` at line 1678, so its `ts` (taken inside the helper at scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:2320) is the post-dispatch moment.
  WHY: The agents.d contract measures wait time up to the `event=granted` `ts`, so unlabel and dispatch latency inflates measured wait and delays the recorded hold start. Severity is disputed: gemini, minimax, luna and glm rate it MAJOR; sonnet rates it NIT (confidence 2), saying the inflation is small and bounded and the decision is unaffected. The highest, MAJOR→high, is used.
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:1672 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `no_waiter` metric call omits the 8th `holder` argument, so `metric_holder="${8:-${MERGE_LEASE_PR:-}}"` (scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:2311) falls back to the stale global `MERGE_LEASE_PR`. A free lease then logs `holder=<old PR>` while the adjacent `MERGE_LEASE` line shows `pr=-`.
  WHY: Phase 2+ per-base occupancy analysis would count a phantom holder, and `test_no_waiter`/`test_expired_holder` do not assert `holder`. Sonnet notes that passing `""` does not fix it because `${8:-...}` treats empty as unset, so the literal `-` is needed; glm suggests `""`. All reviewers rate it NIT.
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:2434-2466 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: When a PR's own record is `state=held` but expired, `lease_keep_acquired` stays empty and the write stamps `acquired=now` (a fresh hold). The outcome check still uses the pre-write record, so the gate emits `event=renewed hold_s=-` instead of `event=acquired hold_s=0`.
  WHY: The agents.d contract marks a hold's start with `event=acquired`/`event=granted`, so the new hold's start is missed and later `held`/`released` `hold_s` values contradict the absent start event. All flagging reviewers rate it NIT. minimax_minimax-m3 explicitly disputes this finding: it says the behaviour follows the spec (agents.d documents `hold_s=-`) and is locked by an existing test.
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:2362 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `invalid_input` metric in `_merge_lease_gate` omits the `holder` argument and fires before any `_merge_lease_read` in that call, so `holder=` inherits a stale `MERGE_LEASE_PR` from an earlier gate or tick call in the same long-lived shell.
  WHY: The emitted holder points at an unrelated PR or base, which corrupts per-base attribution (observability only). All flagging reviewers rate it NIT.
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:1680 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The grant-failure (`lost_race`/`write_failed`) metric call has 7 positional args, so `holder` falls back to the `MERGE_LEASE_PR` set by the loop's earlier read (the previous released holder).
  WHY: On `lost_race` it reports the wrong PR as the holder of a lease just granted to a third PR, and on `write_failed` it reports a holder that does not exist, which corrupts per-base analysis (observability only, rated NIT).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
(No task gaps reported.)
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:line 1672, `[ "${tick_metric_ok}" = 1 ] && _merge_lease_metric no_waiter "${tick_base}" "" tick lease_free "" 0 || true`; helper fallback at scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh line 2311, `metric_holder="${8:-${MERGE_LEASE_PR:-}}"` | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `no_waiter` metric passes no holder, so it falls back to the global `MERGE_LEASE_PR`. That global is still set after a release (the write at line 1658 leaves it; only `MERGE_LEASE_STATE` is reset at line 1666) and for already-released records (`_merge_lease_read`, pr_checks_lib.sh lines 2123/2130).
  WHY: A free lease emits `holder=<old PR>` while `MERGE_LEASE` shows `pr=-` (e.g. `TickMetrics.test_expired_holder` prints `holder=4`), so phantom holders appear in Phase 2+ analysis. The tests never assert `holder`. Fix: pass the literal `-` as the 8th arg (`""` does not work because of `${8:-...}`).
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:`_merge_lease_gate`, line 2362, `_merge_lease_metric unavailable "${lease_base}" "${lease_pr}" "${lease_mode}" invalid_input || true` | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The `invalid_input` branch returns before any read, and the gate never resets `MERGE_LEASE_PR` (it resets only OUTCOME/REASON/BLOCKER at lines 2351-2353), so `holder=` carries over from a prior call. Long-lived shells such as `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` (lines 27273, 31092, 33207) reach this branch with an empty base via pr_checks_lib.sh lines 1837/1878.
  WHY: The emitted holder belongs to an unrelated earlier PR or base. Fix: pass `"" "" -`.
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:`_merge_lease_gate`, lines 2434-2439, 2450, 2453-2454, 2462-2463 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When the PR's own record is held but expired, the gate starts a new hold (`acquired=now`), yet emits `event=renewed hold_s=-` and no `event=acquired`.
  WHY: This contradicts the agents.d contract (`hold_s` is 0 on acquisition; a hold starts at acquired/granted), and later held/released `hold_s` values are measured from an unannounced start. Fix: `[ "${MERGE_LEASE_OUTCOME}" = "renewed" ] && [ -n "${lease_keep_acquired}" ]`, with the outcome left unchanged.
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:lease write line 1678; `granted` metric lines 1689/1692 after `_merge_lease_unlabel_wait` (line 1686) and `_mt_dispatch_review` (line 1687); ts at pr_checks_lib.sh line 2320 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The grant `ts` is taken after one label DELETE and one workflow dispatch, not when the lease write succeeds.
  WHY: Wait times are inflated by unlabel plus dispatch latency. The reviewer rejects the pass-1 MAJOR rating because the inflation is small and bounded and the decision is unaffected. Fix: capture `date -u +%s` after line 1683, or document the timing.
- Missing context: the binding plan `docs/plans/merge-lease-parallel-merges-plan.md` (Phase 1, D1-D9, §18.E) is not in the checkout, so metric names, fields and sink were not checked against it. TASK COMPLETENESS: NONE (all deliverables present).
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS: 3 one-line fixes (1672 append `-`, 2362 append `"" "" -`, 2462 add `-n lease_keep_acquired`). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1 (3 related items)
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:lines 1672 (tick `no_waiter`) and similar logic throughout | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Metric calls lack the 8th `holder` argument and fall back to the stale global `MERGE_LEASE_PR`.
  WHY: A `no_waiter` event may report the PR of a previously released or expired lease, i.e. a phantom holder for a free lease.
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:Lines 2435-2463 (within `_merge_lease_gate`) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: An expired lease re-acquired by the same PR is emitted as `event=renewed hold_s=-` instead of `event=acquired hold_s=0`.
  WHY: Treating a fresh re-acquisition as a renewal confuses downstream analysis that expects acquired/granted to mark the start of a hold.
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:Lines 1684-1692 (within `_mt_merge_lease_tick`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `granted` metric is emitted after `_mt_dispatch_review` instead of at `_merge_lease_write`.
  WHY: The timestamp includes the dispatch duration, which inflates wait and delays the recorded lease start.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:1678 (successful _merge_lease_write); 1684-1692 (metric emit after _mt_dispatch_review); helper ts capture at scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh ~2317 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `event=granted` is emitted after `_mt_dispatch_review` returns, so `ts` reflects the post-dispatch moment, not the grant.
  WHY: The agents.d wait-time definition then includes the `_mt_unlabel_wait` + `_mt_dispatch_review` round trip, and the timing contradicts the adjacent `MERGE_LEASE` line, which is logged at write time.
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:1672 (the no_waiter emit: `_merge_lease_metric no_waiter "${tick_base}" "" tick lease_free "" 0 || true`) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: 7 args, so `holder` defaults to the `MERGE_LEASE_PR` populated by `_merge_lease_read` from the released/expired record. The output is `holder=<old PR>` while `MERGE_LEASE` shows `pr=-`.
  WHY: This corrupts per-base occupancy, hold and grant counts. `tests/test_merge_lease.py::TickMetrics::test_no_waiter` does not assert holder.
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:2362 (the invalid_input emit: `_merge_lease_metric unavailable "${lease_base}" "${lease_pr}" "${lease_mode}" invalid_input || true`) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: 5 args, so `holder` falls back to a `MERGE_LEASE_PR` carried over from a previous gate call, on a path that never read the record.
  WHY: A phantom holder points at an unrelated PR (observability only).
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:1680 (the grant-failure emit: `_merge_lease_metric "$([ "${tick_rc}" -eq 3 ] && echo lost_race || echo write_failed)" "${tick_base}" "${tick_first}" tick grant "" "${tick_waiters}" || true`) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: 7 args, so `holder` falls back to the previous released holder, unrelated to the race winner (never re-read) or to the absent holder on write_failed.
  WHY: On lost_race it reports the losing PR as the holder, and on write_failed a nonexistent holder, which corrupts per-base analysis (observability only).
- Editor note: move the `granted` metric to just after the successful `_merge_lease_write`, pass an explicit `-` holder at 1672, 1680 and 2362, tighten `test_no_waiter`, and add a gate `invalid_input` test asserting `holder=-`. The reviewer considers the renewed-without-acquired case per spec (agents.d documents `hold_s=-`, and an existing test locks it), so not a defect. TASK COMPLETENESS: NONE.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

  PROBLEM: The successful `granted` metric is emitted only after `_mt_dispatch_review` finishes.
  WHY: `event=granted` is the documented wait endpoint, but its `ts` comes after dispatch rather than at the lease write at line 1678, so dispatch latency is included in the wait.
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:1672; holder fallback in scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:2311 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `no_waiter` metric omits holder and falls back to the mutable `MERGE_LEASE_PR` global.
  WHY: After a read or release the global keeps the record's PR, so a free base logs `holder=<old PR>` instead of `holder=-`.
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:2435-2440, 2453-2465 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: A same-PR expired held lease gets a fresh acquisition (empty `lease_keep_acquired`), but the gate emits `event=renewed`.
  WHY: The outcome check uses the pre-write `MERGE_LEASE_PR`/`MERGE_LEASE_STATE`, so the metric reports `hold_s=-` with no documented `acquired` event.
- TASK COMPLETENESS: NONE. HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS: NONE. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 0
